ns2:section.sectionText: The Rhetoric of the Black Freedom Movement 1948-1984 explores the languages that justified equal rights for African Americans leading to, during, and shortly after the classical phase of the civil rights movement. It attends to movement rhetoric, white supremacist discourse, legislative and political debates as well as some of the extensive secondary rhetorical literature on civil rights. In particular, the course will (tentatively) proceed through a series of mini-rhetorical biographies, exploring key figures in the movement and beyond.
